news.title: Apple says it’s tightening macOS ‘Full Disk Access’ controls due to new risks from AI agents
news.summary_raw: Apple says it will add new controls around macOS’s Full Disk Access permission, warning that increasingly capable AI agents make broad access to users’ files, messages, mail, and browsing history riskier.
news.summary: Apple is tightening macOS Full Disk Access controls in response to AI agents’ increasing ability to exploit broad file system permissions. This change introduces new security requirements for macOS endpoints that IT teams must review promptly.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Immediately log into your MDM console and verify that the new macOS Full Disk Access restrictions are enabled for all managed devices. S2: Failure to enforce these settings could allow AI-driven malware to read sensitive user data, increasing data breach risk. S3: The change will most directly affect your Apple device fleet managed via JumpCloud and your endpoint security policies in CrowdStrike.

news.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology
news.summary_raw:
Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions.
The post Introducing Q
news.summary: Microsoft Research has unveiled Quine, a multimodal AI system aimed at modeling complex biological systems across various scales and modalities. The tool is designed to enable scientists to computationally explore vast hypothesis spaces and prioritize experimental directions.
news.enterprise_use: Quine is an academic research platform and does not directly interact with or affect the IT engineer’s existing tools or infrastructure.

news.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
news.summary_raw:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.
The post Forecasting space weather risks on power grids appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed a machine learning system that forecasts space‑weather events, predicting potential damage to power grids and GPS systems 30–60 minutes before storms hit. The technology aims to give utilities and satellite operators early warning to mitigate infrastructure risk.
news.enterprise_use: Check your organization’s IT infrastructure for any dependencies on GPS or satellite‑based services that might be affected by space‑weather. Evaluate whether your cloud or on‑prem monitoring tools can ingest the forecast data to trigger pre‑emptive alerts or fail‑over procedures. Document the potential impact on critical services and schedule a review in the next quarter.
